subject: Identity gateway: SSO & SCIM sync plan for private control plane
messages:
From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private control plane: SSO / SCIM kickoff and network constraints

Hi Priyom and Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. ACME's security team has reviewed Redwood's private control plane options and we want to align on a minimal-risk integration path for SSO and user provisioning. A few constraints on our side:

- All auth traffic must terminate inside our VPC (no public IdP callbacks).
- We use Okta as the IdP with SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0 provisioning.
- We require a short-lived service account for API sync; keys rotate every 30 days.
- SOC2 auditors will want the mapping of Okta groups -> Redwood roles.

Can you share proposed flow (SAML assertion endpoint, SCIM endpoint placement, and any identity gateway you recommend) plus a list of artifacts you need from ACME? I'm attaching our IdP metadata and the initial SCIM schema we expect to use.

Attachments: acme-idp-metadata.xml (attached), acme-scim-profile.json (attached)

Best,
Alice
Security Ops, ACME Corp
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private control plane: SSO / SCIM kickoff and network constraints

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear constraints and the metadata. High level proposal below; I'll loop in infra for details.

Proposal overview:
1) Identity gateway (lightweight in-customer VPC component) — we recommend deploying a small, customer-owned identity gateway (container) inside ACME's VPC. This component proxies SAML assertions and hosts the SCIM endpoint so all identity traffic never leaves the VPC.

2) Control plane trust model — Redwood control plane (private deployment variant) will establish a mutual TLS connection to the identity gateway. mTLS certs are provisioned during onboarding and can be rotated via API.

3) SCIM provisioning — SCIM will be consumed by the gateway and then forwarded into Redwood's private control plane over the mTLS channel. We support SCIM bulk and delta patch.

4) Role mapping — we will provide a mapping template for Okta group -> Redwood IAM role. We'll store mappings in the private control plane; changes will be auditable and exportable for SOC2.

Artifacts we need from ACME:
- Signed SAML metadata (your attachment looks good)
- SCIM attribute list and canonical external ids you use for groups
- VPC CIDR and security group rules for the gateway (eg inbound from control plane IPs)
- Preferred rotation cadence for mTLS certs and a contact for cert ops

I've attached a rough network diagram and an initial mutual action plan. Next steps: schedule a technical deep-dive with Dev and Marcus; I'll propose times.

Attachments: network-diagram.png, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

- Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private control plane: SSO / SCIM kickoff and network constraints

Adding a few technical notes from infra:

- Identity gateway implementation: we can provide a Docker image (light, ~150MB) that exposes two endpoints internally: /saml/callback (POST) and /scim/v2/ (HTTPS). It will accept connections only over the VPC private subnet.

- mTLS: we need ACME to accept an initial CA cert or exchange signed certs via a secure out-of-band channel (we can use SFTP or their SSM). We also support HashiVault for PMEM if they want automatic rotation.

- Firewall rules: ACME's egress rules must allow outbound to Redwood control plane egress IPs on 443. Inbound rules only required for our control plane to reach the gateway on the agreed port (we recommend 8443).

- Audit logs: gateway will emit structured audit events to a syslog endpoint you provide; alternatively we can forward a daily zipped audit bundle to an S3 bucket in your account.

Engineering ask: Marcus, can we draft the SCIM validation schema we will apply server-side so ACME can test with their Okta provisioning job?

- Dev
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private control plane: SSO / SCIM kickoff and network constraints

Dev — I'll take point on the SCIM validation and the group->role mapping template. Initial checklist below; I'll attach the schema in the follow-up: 

SCIM validation checklist (draft):
- Required attributes: id (uuid), userName, emails[type=work], active
- Group sync: id, displayName, members[] with externalId mapping
- Accepts PATCH operations for membership changes
- Rejects unknown custom attributes by default; provide opt-in list for extras

Role mapping template (preview):
- okta:Engineering -> redwood:developer
- okta:Data-Science -> redwood:ml-engineer
- okta:Admin -> redwood:admin (requires approval in console)

I will post the initial scim-schema-v2.json and a sample validation test harness link tomorrow morning.

- Marcus
Applied ML / Access Team, Redwood Inference
